title: The Free Time Common to All Workers

concept.title: Merge the busy times; the holes between the merged blocks are the free time
body: Several workers have meetings, and all the meetings are given in one list in any order (a meeting is the time from `s` up to `e`; two meetings of **different** workers may overlap, since they are different people). A moment is **common free time** when **nobody** is in a meeting. Find the **stretches of common free time between the first meeting start and the last meeting end** (time before the first meeting and after the last one is not counted). For the meetings `1-3, 2-4, 6-7, 9-12, 10-11` the free stretches are `4-6` and `7-9`.

The moment is free when it is covered by **no meeting at all**, so the question is about the **union** of the meetings, no matter who attends each. Sort the meetings by the start, and keep `end`, the farthest end seen so far. When the next meeting starts **after** `end`, the time from `end` to this start is a free stretch (the length is positive, so something really is free). Then update `end = max(end, e)`.

A meeting that starts exactly when the previous block ends leaves no gap (the free stretch would have zero length). It is important to take the maximum of the ends: a long early meeting can hide many short ones. The sort makes the algorithm O(n log n); the gaps come out in increasing order.

statement: `n` meetings of all workers are given in one list. A meeting is the time from `s` up to `e`. Print all the stretches of positive length between the earliest start and the latest end during which no meeting takes place. First print the number of stretches, then the stretches in increasing order, one per line (`from to`).
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of meetings of all the workers together.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `s` and `e`: a meeting that occupies the time from `s` up to `e`.
outputFormat: The first line has the number of free stretches `m` (possibly 0).
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers: the start and the end of a free stretch.

examples.note: The second meeting starts when the first ends: no free time, 0.

hints: Only the union of all the meetings matters.
Sort the meetings by the start and keep the farthest end so far.
A gap exists when the next start is greater than the farthest end.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
meetings = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: The meetings are sorted by start; the farthest end so far is tracked, and every time a meeting starts after it, the stretch between them is reported as free time.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n) for the output.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
meetings = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

meetings.sort()
gaps = []
end = meetings[0][1]
for i in range(1, n):
    s, e = meetings[i]
    if s > end:
        gaps.append(str(end) + " " + str(s))
    if e > end:
        end = e
print(len(gaps))
if gaps:
    print("\n".join(gaps))
